purpose: Sign and push a tagged image's trust data via Notary. Requires a delegation key in the local trust store (`~/.docker/trust/private/`) and the public-key counterpart already added to the Notary server for the GUN. Overwrites remote trust metadata. Equivalent to `docker push` with `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1`.

flags.name: --local
flags.doc: Sign a locally tagged image (don't first push to registry).

examples.expected_output: Signing and pushing trust data for local image ...; Successfully signed registry.example.com/admin/demo:1
`docker push` with auto-sign — equivalent to `docker trust sign`
examples.scenario: opt-in DCT signing on a regular push pipeline

purpose: Display Notary trust data for a tag or repository: signers, signed tags, key IDs, signing thresholds. JSON-formatted by default; `--pretty` for human output.

flags.name: --pretty
flags.doc: Human-friendly output (signed tags + signer name + tagging key ID).

examples.expected_output: SIGNED TAG / DIGEST / SIGNERS table; Administrative keys + Repository Key + Root Key listing
examples.scenario: verify before pulling — confirm the digest is signed by an expected signer

examples.expected_output: JSON dump of all signed tags + signers in the repo
examples.scenario: feed into a policy script that gates which images can be pulled

purpose: Remove trust data for a specific tag (or all tags via `--yes` on a repo). After revocation, pulls with `DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1` reject the tag. Cannot be undone without re-signing.

flags.name: -y, --yes
flags.doc: Skip confirmation prompt; required when targeting a whole repo (no tag).

examples.scenario: un-sign a compromised tag (force re-build + re-sign with new digest)

examples.expected_output: Successfully deleted signature for registry.example.com/admin/demo (all tags)
examples.scenario: emergency: pull all signed tags from a compromised repo

purpose: Manage delegation keys in the local trust store. `generate` creates a new keypair (private under `~/.docker/trust/private/`, public to cwd); `load` imports an existing private key. Both prompt for a passphrase to encrypt the on-disk key. The companion to `docker trust signer add` which uploads the public side to Notary.

flags.name: --name
flags.doc: Logical name for this delegation (used in `docker trust signer add` and `docker trust inspect`). Required.

flags.name: --dir
flags.doc: Output dir for the generated public key (`<name>.pub`). Default: cwd.

examples.expected_output: Generating key for jeff...; Successfully generated and loaded private key. Corresponding public key available: ./jeff.pub
examples.scenario: first-time setup of a CI signer key

examples.invocation: docker trust key load key.pem --name jeff
examples.expected_output: Loading key from "key.pem"...; Successfully imported key from key.pem
examples.scenario: import a key generated by an external CA into the local trust store

examples.invocation: docker trust signer add --key cert.pem jeff registry.example.com/admin/demo
examples.expected_output: Adding signer "jeff" to registry.example.com/admin/demo... (prompts for repo key passphrase)
examples.scenario: register the public key with the Notary server for a specific repo (companion command)
